question: Your team uses Claude Code to write an architecture overview of a payment service. Subagents each read one kind of source: decision records, incident postmortems, and exported dashboard reports, all bulk-copied into the repository last month. Each subagent's structured output gives a claim, the document name, an excerpt, and a date taken from the file's last-modified time. The overview presents latency figures measured years apart as conflicting current measurements. Which change best fixes this problem?

options.text: Require each subagent to fill the date field with the source's publication or data collection date, such as a report's measurement period, not the file timestamp.
options.reason: The guide calls for publication or data collection dates in structured outputs so that temporal differences are not misread as contradictions; a bulk-copy timestamp makes every source look equally recent.

options.text: Instruct the synthesis step to keep only the figure whose source file has the most recent last-modified time whenever two figures disagree.
options.reason: The timestamps all reflect last month's bulk copy, so they say nothing about when data was measured, and the guide warns against arbitrarily selecting one value.

options.text: Have each subagent drop the date field and return a longer excerpt instead, so that the synthesis step can infer when each figure was measured.
options.reason: The guide requires subagents to include dates explicitly in structured outputs; leaving the synthesis step to infer dates from excerpts removes the field that enables correct temporal interpretation.

options.text: Move every pair of disagreeing latency figures into a contested-findings section of the overview, with each figure attributed to its source document.
options.reason: The figures are not truly contested; they differ because they were measured at different times, and without correct dates the temporal difference is still misread as a contradiction.
